PullRequest.Title: Add commands to hide the editor area for the chat part
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Infrastructure for a chat area that can take the place of the editor area. With no feature enabling a chat area, nothing changes: the new context keys are false and the new item is hidden.

- `IWorkbenchLayoutService.isEditorHiddenByChat` and `setEditorHiddenByChat`: while the chat part is visible, the editor area can be hidden so that the chat part takes its width (its layout priority is High while the editor area is hidden this way). Opening an editor, hiding the chat part, and maximizing or moving the panel show the editor area again. The state persists with the layout state and applies again after a reload while the chat part shows.
- "View: Toggle Editor Area Visibility" (`workbench.action.toggleEditorVisibility`) hides or shows the editor area for the chat part while the chat part is visible or the editor area is hidden by it; otherwise it keeps maximizing the panel. View > Appearance gets an "Editor Area" item under the same condition.
- Context keys `chatPartVisible` and `editorAreaHiddenByChat`, kept correct at startup (the layout creates the chat part visible without an event) and on each change; `chatPartEnabled` is declared here and set by the feature that enables the chat area.
- The maximize action of the secondary side bar (title action, Maximize and Toggle Maximized commands) is hidden and disabled while `chatPartEnabled`; Restore stays.

Stack and merge order: independent of other PRs, merges after #348317 and #348346. Before the PRs that enable the chat area merge, the `chatPartEnabled` binding (currently in the banner PR, in `EditorWindowChatPartService`) moves into #348309, which owns that service.

How to test:
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/contextkeys.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/layout.test.ts --browser chromium`: 24 passing.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: no errors; `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed source files: clean.
- Edge cases covered by `layout.test.ts`: toggle and width, no chat part, reveal on editor open, hiding the chat part (also with a maximized secondary side bar), reload, secondary side bar maximize and restore.
- Manually, the command needs a window with a chat part (the Agents chat part).


**Sweep merge (2a017024e85):** merged origin/main `776b518e720` (clean merge, no behaviour change).
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`: passed
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: 0 errors
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run <each changed src/**/*.test.ts> --browser chromium`: 24 passing, 0 failing


### Update 3c0c2896741

- Focus goes to the chat part, not the hidden editor, while the editor is hidden for the chat part.
- A reload without a chat part, with the secondary side bar maximized, keeps the editor hidden until it is restored.
- Validation: `layout.test.ts` 24 passing (the two new tests fail without the change), `pnpm run typecheck-client` 0 errors, `pnpm run valid-layers-check` ok.

### Follow-ups

- Persist and restore the pre-hide editor and chat split coherently across reload and window resize, with a resize, hide, reload, show roundtrip test.


### Update 963604a55fe

- The chat part focus branch of `focus()` applies only while the main window is active, so an active auxiliary editor window keeps its editor focused.
- Validation: `layout.test.ts` 24 passing (the new expectation fails without the guard), `pnpm run typecheck-client` 0 errors, `pnpm run valid-layers-check` ok.



## Update

- Merged main (e0da8291880).
- ChatPartEnabledContext is bound from the layout; new onDidChangeChatPartVisibility event fires once per change and drives ChatPartVisibleContext; mnemonic reverted (b538207e3aa).

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or reload a workbench with or without a registered chat part, including persisted editor-hidden and maximized-secondary-sidebar states.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: LayoutStateModel.load and createGridDescriptor synchronously construct the initial grid. The new whenRestored callback updates four context keys after restoration; it does not add an awaited prerequisite to restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the cached chat-layout string and parse its small version/visibility/size object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one parse when a chat part exists; now at most two when EDITOR_HIDDEN_BY_CHAT is set and a chat part exists. No transcript or editor collection is parsed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One existing chat-layout read/parse during grid descriptor creation; no hidden-by-chat normalization read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous initial-grid construction, but constant-sized and performed once per layout creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the existing initialized storage cache, populated through the existing bulk storage-load path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional boolean-key cache lookup. No additional getItems IPC or database request per key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same storage initialization loaded workspace state in bulk; the layout iterated one fewer fixed state key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new lookup is local; existing storage initialization boundaries are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One window, at most one chat part, a fixed set of workbench parts, and a constant-sized persisted layout object.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous descriptor construction, followed by one promise callback after restoration; no new parallel resource creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Missing chat-layout state returns a default without retrying a remote operation. Both present and absent storage keys are resolved from the initialized cache. No new cache or dynamically growing keyspace is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced initialization, cached storage reads, normalization, grid construction, and restoration callback.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Startup timings were not measured; added work is demonstrably bounded and independent of workspace files, editor history, or chat history.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: only bounded flag handling and at most one extra small cached-state parse.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle editor-area visibility for a visible chat part, then resize the window or return focus to the workbench.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command synchronously updates hidden-state flags and chat layout priority, changes editor grid visibility, and transfers focus when necessary. Window resize uses the existing grid/content layout path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update DOM visibility and dimensions and lay out the existing editor/chat contents; read cached content-border geometry when required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded number of grid passes per requested visibility transition, with existing content layout costs. The priority getter does not create another layout pass or enumerate chat history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor-toggle command maximized/restored the panel; ordinary grid resizing and chat-content layout already existed. This change adds the requested chat-specific visibility transition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the UI thread during the requested layout operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User-triggered visibility changes and resize events; fixed outer workbench grid, with pre-existing inner editor/chat rendering costs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI operations; no asynchronous task fan-out, network requests, subprocesses, or per-editor persistence calls were added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Equal hidden-by-chat requests return early. Existing splitview caches hidden sizes; ChatHostPart retains its existing border-edge cache and invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the action through setEditorHiddenByChat, setEditorHidden, grid visibility, ChatHostPart priority/layout, and focusContent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Content-layout cost depends on the active editors and chat content, but no changed collection-scaling or repeated resize mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: work implements the requested visible layout change, and the changed resize priority is a constant-time getter.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or activate a main-window editor while the editor area is hidden for chat.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing visible-editor/group-activation listeners check current visibility and active editors, then reveal the editor once through setEditorHiddenByChat(false). Subsequent events return when the editor is visible.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible-editor changes and group activations; no new iteration over files, tabs, or history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event handling; automatic editor opens do not restore a maximized secondary sidebar. No new editor-resolution or filesystem/network operation is called by the added branch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing in-memory layout state provides the guard. Clearing the hidden-by-chat flag prevents repeated reveal work on subsequent events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected listener registration, guards, editor visibility handling, and grid propagation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual editor-opening and layout duration is content-dependent; those existing costs do not establish an added boundary or new multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added branch substitutes the appropriate bounded reveal operation for existing panel/sidebar restoration behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Maximize or move the panel, close the chat part, or restore a maximized secondary sidebar after chat hid the editor.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Layout methods synchronously reconcile editor/chat flags and grid visibility. Panel maximization can reveal the editor before hiding it with chat; moving the panel reveals the editor before grid rearrangement. Existing pane-composite opening remains conditional on showing an inactive panel/sidebar.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform grid visibility/layout passes and, where already required, restore an existing pane composite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded passes over the fixed workbench layout per explicit transition. Existing openViewContainer tries the requested/default/first visible container sequentially, not one operation per editor or chat item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Panel movement/maximization and secondary-sidebar restoration already changed multiple grid views. Hidden-by-chat reconciliation and its temporary editor reveal are new; the pane-composite opening helper and fallback behavior are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Grid work is synchronous on the UI path; existing pane-composite opening is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User layout commands and at most one chat part; inner content determines existing layout cost, not the number of persisted sessions or workspace resources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous grid mutations; secondary-sidebar transitions retain their reentrancy guard. No new subprocess, network, filesystem, or IPC fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cached visible sizes and the existing secondary-sidebar transition guard are preserved. Chat visibility events fire only when the backing boolean changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded additional visibility transitions and unchanged pane-composite call cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A temporary reveal adds layout work during panel maximization, but no evidence establishes a significant regression beyond this infrequent intentional state-reconciliation path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable performance bug: new work is bounded to the requested layout transition, without a new hot-loop or resource-scaling mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Maintain command/menu context keys and persist layout state, including windows without chat and the sessions workbench.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Context-key initialization and updates are synchronous and local. The new workspace boolean is saved by the existing onWillSaveState callback; durable storage flushing remains outside the interaction critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist one additional workspace boolean through cached, deduplicated storage and the existing batched database update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixed key, at most one pending value per flush; unchanged values are suppressed. It joins the existing workspace update batch rather than adding one IPC per visibility event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same save callback, delayed flush, and batched updateItems boundary persisted the other layout keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runtime workspace flag updates only change the state model cache. Existing deferred storage flush owns IPC/database work; no new await blocks layout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One extra persisted boolean, three context keys, and one registered chat-visibility listener per handler/window; no unbounded collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local synchronous context updates, one restoration continuation, and existing throttled storage flushes; no concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ContextKeyService suppresses events for unchanged values. Storage suppresses unchanged writes and coalesces pending inserts by key. The new emitter/listener are registered for owner disposal; the sessions implementation uses Event.None and constant-returning methods.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced context change suppression, listener ownership, workspace-only runtime caching, storage deduplication/coalescing, and updateItems serialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu-consumer reaction time is not measured, but added keys/events are fixed-size and state changes are deduplicated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable retention, cache, serialization, or boundary-fanout regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 11 changed files and every diff page. Traced startup/restoration, chat/editor visibility and resize, editor-open restoration, panel/sidebar transitions, context propagation, disposal ownership, and cached/batched persistence. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance bug or concrete shipped performance-regression fix was established; no findings submitted.
